text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- After six years with no charter flights Esbjerg Airport in southern Denmark sees its first charter aircraft taking off Sunday for Tunisia with 177 passengers.

--- For the first time in five years Danes buy more goods in Germany than Germans buy in Denmark. If the trend of the first nine months of 1996 continues, Danes shopping south of the border will give a deficit of 150 million crowns.

--- Danish researchers have developed a new DNA like material which is to store more data than present computer hard discs. The Risoe government research centre, west of Copenhagen, has already taken out a patent for the new material named DNO which is said to be the base of future storing of illustrations and information.

--- Danish pork producers had total turnover of 14.5 billion crowns in 1995, almost 300 million crowns more than in 1994. Pork industry representatives say that price increases in their favour were better than expected and the main reason for the 1995 result.
